ctx.x: waiting and now it’s like 5 or 6:00 and the guys were getting hungry. So the manager was the white guy, Frenchie — excuse me, the ginger ale, it’s human, it’s real — so we said you know we just passed a diner about a hundred feet back there. So the guy that sold the programs, Frenchie and myself, we went there to get some food. We sat at the counter, we ate, and then we took out five or six, I don’t know, for the rest of the guys. I took orders, like when you work in an office in New York, whoever wants coffee,…

nine feet in the air. Like there was a balcony, a bandstand about eight or nine feet up, with a railing. I don’t even know if it had a railing, with an upright piano that was on a slant. Because the floor slanted this way toward the thing. So I went up on the bandstand and Bob says to me, “you’d better get those two girls and bring them up here, because it could get rough.” It could get rough. I says okay. They were both blondes too. I said, “hey girls, up here” so they come up and they sat on the bandstand all…
Well you’ve got an education then.
